chapter: Old bandleaders, drummers and Edgewater years
title: Ray Baduc's age, drummers Frank liked, and a three-piece job
summary: Frank gives opinions of drummers, jokes about Godfrey playing drums and vibes, and a job where guests kept interrupting.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Do you remember when Ray worked for Beiersdorfer?

When Ray... Ray Paduca. Ray Paduca. Ray Paduca. Ray Paduca. Yeah, he was out there on the lakefront. Yeah, yeah. He was... Ray was quite young. How old is he now? Would you give an idea? He's gotta be 80 years old. He's 80.
Yeah, he just turned 80. He just turned 80.

Well, I thought he was a couple of years younger than me. But Ray, we thought half a time, a dozen times over. After Crum got finished, we didn't know him. Excuse me. I'm sorry, Ray. If you ever hear this.
We'll restrict that. He wasn't. Yeah. He wasn't the best liked drummer in the world. No, no. His personality, he didn't have a...

He didn't have a big personality. He jigged and he threw the sticks up in the air. He was a clown. And today, he would probably be terrific. Who were the drummers that you did like? I liked Pothead Addy. I liked Von Gammon. Von Gammon. And there was two.

Listen, children do it. I played drums with us. I know you played drums too. I played drums with you too. Yeah, but you played drums with us too, but not very long. You were playing mostly piano and the... No, I played drums at the radio station. Huh? I played drums at the radio station. Yeah, I know. I was a premier percussionist down there. That's right. That's right.
But you were playing vibes up there. You were talking or you were playing piano. . . . .

. . . . There's a funny thing about your comrades there, your, what the hell do you call them, your Jewish friends. He's playing vibes over there and the guy comes over there with his hand and grabs you and saying, how you doing, Godfrey? And here's the guy playing a chorus on the vibes. He did that the other night. Who the hell was that Levy guy? Yeah, I don't know. Yeah, they go up there, he's playing the tune over there, I don't remember what the tune was, and he's going along there and the guy comes up and he sees Godfrey and Godfrey knows all those Jews up there, you know the question about it, and they come over there to shake hands with him. The man's playing a good kid, waiting until he's finished. He's got to grab his hand there and Godfrey's got to put the other one down and there is Ken Carr and I. I didn't stop playing. You know, Ken says, Frank, he says, did you know we had a two piece van up here?
That's the trouble I get for booking a three piece job.
Yeah, well, no, the job was alright, there was nothing wrong with the job. They don't talk to you when you're not playing.
That's right. Well, I know too many of those people, I knew all of them. In fact, I was... Well, you went to school with all of them. I went to school with half of them.
